title: Mljet, Croatia Cost Guide 2026: Budget Travel Breakdown
metaDescription: Explore Mljet's 2026 travel costs. This guide details daily expenses for accommodation, food, transport, and park entry for budget to mid-range travelers.
content:
## Accommodation Costs
Standard guesthouse rooms in Mljet range from €40-€70 per night during peak season. Apartments with kitchenettes are available for €60-€100. Hotels, primarily in Pomena or Polače, start at €100+. Early booking is crucial for better rates.

## National Park Entry & Activities
*   Mljet National Park entry fee: Approximately €15-€20 (120-150 HRK equivalent) per adult for a one-day ticket, including boat ride to St. Mary's Island. Multi-day passes offer better value.
*   Kayak or bicycle rental: Expect €10-€15 for a half-day. This is a worthwhile activity.

## Dining Expenses
*   Casual eateries and bakeries offer meals for €8-€15. A pizza or pasta dish averages €12. 
*   Mid-range restaurants: Main courses are typically €18-€30. Seafood can exceed €30 per dish.
*   Grocery store purchases significantly reduce food costs; local markets offer fresh produce.

## Transportation on Mljet
*   Ferry from Dubrovnik or Korčula: Passenger catamarans cost €10-€20 per person one-way, depending on the route. Car ferries are more expensive and limited.
*   Island bus service connects villages, costing €3-€5 per ride. Schedules are infrequent outside peak season.
*   Scooter rental: €35-€50 per day, providing flexibility to explore the island.

## Opinionated Insight
Some small local restaurants, particularly outside the main tourist hubs, deliver better value and a more authentic dining experience than their more visible counterparts in Pomena or Polače.

faq.question: Is Mljet expensive compared to other Croatian islands?
faq.answer: Mljet's costs for accommodation and dining are comparable to mid-range Croatian islands like Korčula, slightly less expensive than Hvar or Dubrovnik.

faq.question: What is the best way to get to Mljet?
faq.answer: The most common way to reach Mljet is by catamaran ferry from Dubrovnik or Split, with connections often via Korčula or Hvar, depending on the season.

faq.question: How many days are sufficient for Mljet?
faq.answer: Three to four days are sufficient to explore the Mljet National Park thoroughly, visit other parts of the island, and enjoy its natural surroundings.

quickAnswer: A budget-conscious traveler in Mljet can expect to spend €70-€100 daily in 2026, covering guesthouse accommodation, local groceries, public transport, and National Park entry. A mid-range experience, including private rooms, restaurant meals, and some rental transport, typically costs €120-€200 per day.
